messages:
maria: Heads-up — ap-southeast1 GPU pool is hitting provisioning failures, ~40 Pending pods in the last 15m. :eyes:

devon: seeing the same. nodes report high disk write stalls and OOM-like eviction on kubelet when we try to schedule kata/gpu jobs.

kai: I pulled node metrics — local nvme write amplification and scrub backlog spike after the 5.12.18 kernel push at 03:00 UTC. I think the trim/workqueue scheduling change regressed perf.

maria: any evidence it's kernel-related vs workload change?

kai: timeline aligns with kernel rollout to ap-southeast1 infra pool. Before rollout scrub queue avg < 5%, after -> 70-90% on many hosts. sample iostat/log excerpt:```
$ ssh gnode-az1-072
# iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  1420.00  192.00 36000.00   0.00    0.00  98.5
````

devon: also saw kernel logs: `nvme: trim_sched backlog overrun` spam and `nvme_core: rate_limit=0` messages.

sre-bot: ALERT ap-southeast1: nvme_trim_scheduler backlog > 80% (30 hosts). Incident created: INC-2026-137

ops-anna: Reverting kernel is heavy. Can we throttle the scrub/trim rate or move ephemeral cleaner to off-peak? Might be faster to stop aggressive trim on ephemeral pool.

maria: thoughts on immediate mitigation? We are losing ~1.5k GPU minutes so far. Cost & SLO pain.

kai: quick mitigation options: 1) disable async trim on ephemeral volumes 2) reduce janitor concurrency 3) pin new nodes to older kernel until fix. I'm for 1+3 as fast path.

devon: I can push a daemonic sysctl change via cs-agent to the pool:```
# throttle trim by toggling kernel flag (canary):
echo 0 > /sys/module/nvme_core/parameters/trim_async
# or reduce janitor parallelism
kubectl -n infra patch ds ephemeral-janitor --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"janitor","env":[{"name":"PARALLELISM","value":"2"}] }]}}}}'
```

ops-anna: Patch prepared. Recommend canary 3 nodes in ap-southeast1-a, monitor nvme backlog and GPU pending.

deploy-bot: deploy started: cs-agent config change -> ap-southeast1-a (3 nodes) by devops/devon. ID: dpl-7782 :rocket:

maria: running health check: if backlog drops under 30% in 10m we'll roll to remaining nodes. If not, revert.

kai: FYI long-term we should add a kernel unit test for trim scheduler under heavy write-amplification patterns and add telemetry for nvme_trim_latency in console.

devon: can confirm canary done, backlog on those nodes dropped 78% -> 22% within 6m, GPU pending cleared for those nodes.

maria: great. ops-anna can you coord with infra releases to pin next batch and open a rollback PR for the kernel rollout? Add cost estimate to the incident for lost GPU minutes.

ops-anna: on it. Opening PR and scheduling a controlled rollback / partial hold for the rest of ap-southeast1. Adding cost calc to INC-2026-137. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks team. We'll keep monitoring. Follow-ups: kernel regression ticket + scrub throttling config as a permanent safety valve.

devon: adding runbook note: if nvme_trim_scheduler backlog > 50% -> throttle janitor, disable async trim, escalate to oncall.

sre-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-137 updated: mitigation applied, status: monitoring.
